title: Babbage's Theorem: C(2p-1, p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p²)
description: Proves Babbage's theorem: C(2p-1, p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) for prime p ≥ 3, via Vandermonde's identity. Key step: C(2p, p) = Σ C(p,k)² ≡ 2 (mod p²) since middle terms vanish (p | C(p,k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ p-1). 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Babbage's theorem (1819): C(2p-1, p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) for prime p ≥ 3. Wolstenholme's theorem (1862) strengthens this to C(2p-1, p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p³) for p ≥ 5. Babbage's result follows from Vandermonde's identity and the divisibility p | C(p,k).
overview.problemStatement: Prove Babbage's theorem C(2p-1, p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) using Vandermonde's identity.
overview.proofStrategy: Vandermonde: C(2p,p) = Σ_{k=0}^{p} C(p,k)². Middle terms 1≤k≤p-1: p | C(p,k) → p² | C(p,k)². So C(2p,p) ≡ C(p,0)² + C(p,p)² = 1+1 = 2 (mod p²). Since C(2p,p) = 2·C(2p-1,p-1), cancel 2 (as p is odd).
keyInsights: **Vandermonde's identity**: C(2p,p) = Σ C(p,k)² gives an exact formula for the central binomial coefficient.
**p-divisibility of C(p,k)**: for prime p and 1 ≤ k ≤ p-1, p | C(p,k) — this is why the middle terms vanish mod p².
**Cancellation of 2**: C(2p,p) = 2·C(2p-1,p-1) with gcd(2,p)=1 for odd prime p, so we can cancel 2 from the congruence mod p².

conclusion.implications: Babbage's theorem is a stepping stone to Wolstenholme's theorem (mod p³). The technique — using Vandermonde to reduce to p-divisibility — is paradigmatic.
